Guided by the IB Primary Years Programme (PYP)

Teaching Philosophy

"Learning a new language should be enriching, rewarding and — most importantly — enjoyable for each and every child."

My philosophy is simple: create a supportive, engaging and inclusive environment where students develop English through meaningful inquiry. Five ideas guide everything I plan and teach:

Agency & Differentiation

Every learner is different, so it stands to reason that every lesson offers different ways to participate such as hands-on, cooperative, small-group and one-to-one learning options.

Authentic Communication

Speaking, listening, reading and writing are conducted in every lesson through pair work, discussion and student presentations.

Meaningful Inquiry

Concept-driven units that are based on skills utilised in the real-world make language a tool for thinking, and give learners genuine ownership and transferability to authentic settings.

A Safe, Caring Community

When learners feel valued they become risk-takers that are not afraif of trying, can persevere and celebrate each other's differences.

International-Mindedness

To me, language opens horizons. This enables me to grow knowledgeable, caring communicators for an increasingly globalised world.

My Full Teaching Philosophy

My teaching philosophy is guided by the IB Primary Years Programme (PYP): creating a supportive, engaging, and inclusive learning environment where students can develop their English language skills through meaningful inquiry. I believe learning a new language should be enriching, rewarding, and most importantly, enjoyable for each and every child.

At the core of my approach is student-centred learning. In the PYP, I value students' individuality, recognising that learners bring different backgrounds, experiences, strengths, and support needs to the classroom. I therefore differentiate instruction and use a range of strategies to reach all learners. These include hands-on activities, interactive games, multimedia, cooperative learning, small-group instruction, and one-on-one support as needed.

I believe that language learning is most effective when students have authentic opportunities to communicate, reflect, and connect. I deliberately plan for frequent practice in speaking, listening, reading, and writing, so students can grow in confidence and in fluency. In line with PYP learning goals, my lessons include regular pair and group work, class discussions, and student presentations. I also encourage students to share their ideas, questions, and perspectives, helping our classroom become a place where diversity is celebrated and understanding is built.

Alongside language development, I focus on nurturing students' overall cognitive, social, and emotional growth. I use age-appropriate, content-rich inquiry topics that connect to students' lives and interests. By engaging with concepts in relevant, real-world contexts, students can see language as a powerful tool for thinking, expressing themselves, and making sense of the world. I firmly believe that when students are able to connect learning to who they are and what they care about, they develop a genuine sense of ownership and motivation.

In every PYP classroom, community matters. I work to create a safe, caring, and inclusive space where students feel valued, respected, and accepted. I aim to be patient, approachable, and committed to building strong relationships. When learners feel secure, they are more willing to take risks, try new strategies, and persevere through challenges.

Ultimately, my teaching philosophy is shaped by the belief that learning English should transform students' learning experiences and broaden their horizons. Through dynamic, inquiry-driven, student-centred teaching that is aligned with the IB PYP, I am dedicated to supporting primary ESL learners to develop the language, confidence, and cultural awareness they need to succeed in and beyond the classroom!

Lesson Showcase

Lesson Plan 1 — PYP Grade 4

A transdisciplinary English language & Science lesson plan.

Reflection

This unit is one of my favourites, and got me thinking as much as it did my students! Learners look into why food is wasted and the effects of their daily choices. Through authentic experiences and guided routines, learners noticed patterns, expressed wonder and connected them to concepts of responsibility and change. The unit captures students' best evidence towards action and agency.

"The Magic Hotpot" — Speaking to Writing (S2W)

Transforming creative chatter into words worth writing down!

Reflection

This unit links Chinese culture to food, sparking inquiry into how familiar story structures can help learners transform oral ideas into written works. Strong language growth led to improvements in descriptive writing and the use oif connectives to sequence events, demonstrating ATLs such as thinking, communication and research.

Looking ahead — my plan of action

Goals

My journey in learning about the IB PYP has been a transformative adventure. Initially, I was hesitant to embrace change, but I quickly realized the importance of evolving my pedagogical approach to better prepare myself and my students for a complex, globalized world. By engaging critically with my practices, I identified areas for self-improvement and reignited my passion for education after two decades of teaching.

This course has allowed me to sharpen my research skills and rekindle my critical and creative thinking abilities. The invaluable feedback from my peers enhanced my collaboration and communication abilities, and self-study helped with my self-management. As I connect my skills and interests to pressing issues like food waste, I understand the significance of my role in driving change within my community and beyond.

The strategies I've learned, such as promoting inquiry-based learning, differentiating instruction, and balancing structure with agency, will guide my teaching practices moving forward. I look forward to implementing these insights in the upcoming academic year, crafting an IB-style program that fosters inquiry, knowledge, and intercultural respect among my students.

Ultimately, my goal is to cultivate a classroom environment that encourages my students to become caring, knowledgeable individuals who contribute positively to society. My commitment to continual growth and collaboration ensures that I will adapt and improve as an educator, fully embracing the challenges and rewards that lie ahead.

Thank you!
